Latin word

maximē

adverb

most, best (with verbs of liking); most of all, above all, especially; most, especially, above all; yes, certainly (willing assent)

In this lexicon

  • best

    also used · classical · Traupman 279

  • especially

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.33.3: maximē puerī; Cic. Off. 1.33: in rē pūblicā maximē cōnservanda sunt jūra bellī (Lewis & Short)

  • most

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.5: suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur; Plin. NH 8.29: animālium maximē ōdēre mūrem; Traupman 347

  • yes

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 609b–609c: Sequere mē ergō hāc intrō. — Maximē.; Plaut. Most. 1009–1009b: operam mihi dā. — Maximē.; Traupman 103: by all means!, maximē!

  • maximē placet: favourite

    classical

  • Tempus maximē est ut …: it’s high time

    classical

  • cum maximē (tum maximē): just

    classical

  • Quid tibi maximē placuit?: what did you like best?

    classical

Examples

  • omnis hīc aetās piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur, maximē puerī, quōs ōtium lūsusque sollicitat

    everyone here, of every age, loves fishing, sailing and swimming too, the boys most of all, tempted by free time and playPlin. Ep. 9.33.3

    In the entry for especially

    but above all, all of you, take care to keep well, if you want me to be wellCic. Fam. 14.18.2

    In the entry for especially

    for each of us is led most by his own interestsCic. Fin. 5.5

    In the entry for most

    of all animals they hate the mouse mostPlin. NH 8.29

    In the entry for most
